english: My brother has a dog.
tip: Russian says have with у (u) plus genitive: у моего брата есть собака (u mayevo brata yest sabaka = my brother has a dog).

english: Instead of tea I want coffee.
tip: вместо (vmesta = instead of) takes the genitive: вместо чая (vmesta chaya), чай (chay) becoming чая.

target: То ли дождь, то ли снег.
english: Either rain or snow.
tip: то ли... то ли (to li... to li) means either... or with a note of uncertainty: то ли дождь (dozhd = rain), то ли снег (sneg = snow).

target: Поезд, на котором мы ехали, опоздал.
english: The train we were on was late.
tip: The preposition sits before который (katoryy = which): на котором мы ехали (na katoram my yekhali = on which we rode), not который alone up front.

english: Whose child is crying?
tip: чей (chey = whose) agrees with the thing owned: чей ребёнок (rebyonak = child) is masculine; use чья (chya) for feminine, чьё (chyo) for neuter.

english: This cake is the most delicious.
tip: A comparative plus всех (vsekh = of all) makes a superlative: вкуснее всех (vkusnee vsekh = tastier than all), meaning the tastiest.

english: This is the worst movie of the year.
tip: худший (khudshiy = worst) is the one-word superlative of плохой (plakhoy = bad); лучший (luchshiy) is its opposite, best.

target: Она такая же умная, как мама.
english: She is as smart as mom.
tip: такой же... как (takoy zhe... kak) means as... as, showing equality: такая же умная, как мама (takaya zhe umnaya, kak mama = as smart as mom).

target: Чем раньше встанешь, тем больше успеешь.
english: The earlier you get up, the more you accomplish.
tip: чем... тем (chem... tem) means the more X, the more Y: чем раньше встанешь, тем больше успеешь (chem ranshe vstanesh, tem bolshe uspeesh).

english: This is my window.
tip: Possessives match the noun owned, not the owner. окно (akno = window) is neuter, so моё (mayo = my), not мой (moy) or моя (maya).

english: Whose umbrella is this?
tip: чей (chey = whose) agrees with the owned thing. зонт (zont = umbrella) is masculine, so чей; a feminine noun takes чья (chya).

english: He loves his job.
tip: свою (svayu = his own) points back to the subject: любит свою работу (lyubit svayu rabotu = loves his own job); его (yevo) could mean someone else's.

english: His work is very important.
tip: его (yevo = his) never changes form. Whatever the noun's gender or case, it stays его: его работа (rabota = work).

english: My parents like to travel.
tip: нравится (nravitsya = is pleasing) puts the liker in the dative: моим родителям (maim raditelyam = my parents). The thing liked is the grammatical subject.

english: We are proud of our city.
tip: гордиться (garditsya = to be proud) takes the instrumental with no preposition: гордимся своим городом (gardimsya svaim goradam = we're proud of our city).

english: In the morning I drink coffee.
tip: Times of day take the instrumental, no preposition: утром (utram = in the morning), from утро (utra). Likewise вечером (vecheram), днём (dnyom), ночью (nochyu).

english: We miss our home.
tip: скучать (skuchat = to miss) uses по (pa) plus the dative: скучаем по своему дому (skuchaem pa svayemu domu = we miss our home).

english: This is what I need.
tip: то, что (to, chto = what) joins a main clause to a relative one: то (to) sits first, что (chto) opens the second, as in то, что мне нужно (mne nuzhna = I need).

english: The dog whose owner left is whining.
tip: чей (chey) also serves as relative 'whose', agreeing with the owned noun: собака, чей хозяин ушёл (sabaka, chey khazyain ushyol = the dog whose owner left).

english: He called to find out the news.
tip: When the subject stays the same, чтобы (chtoby) takes an infinitive: позвонил, чтобы узнать (pazvanil, chtoby uznat = called to find out).

target: Ни он, ни она не знали.
english: Neither he nor she knew.
tip: ни ... ни (ni ... ni = neither ... nor) still needs a negated verb: ни он, ни она не знали (ni on, ni ana ne znali = neither he nor she knew).

target: Вместо того чтобы отдыхать, он работал.
english: Instead of resting, he worked.
tip: вместо того чтобы (vmesta tavo chtoby = instead of) is followed by an infinitive, here отдыхать (atdykhat = to rest).

target: Я звонил, а никто не ответил.
english: I called, but nobody answered.
tip: а (a) joins clauses with a light contrast, softer than 'but': звонил, а никто не ответил (zvanil, a nikto ne atvetil = called, but nobody answered).

target: Дом, в котором мы живём, старый.
english: The house in which we live is old.
tip: который (katoryy = which) takes its gender from the noun it replaces but its case from its own clause: в котором (v katoram) is prepositional, matching дом (dom = house).

target: Мы поедем, если будет хорошая погода.
english: We will go if the weather is good.
tip: Russian uses the future in both halves of a real future condition: поедем, если будет (payedem, yesli budet = we'll go if it is), where English keeps the present.

target: Он всегда носит с собой свой зонт.
english: He always carries his umbrella with him.
tip: с собой (s saboy = with oneself) is the reflexive 'with him/her': носит с собой (nosit s saboy = carries with him).

target: Мало того что опоздал, ещё и забыл документы.
english: Not only did someone arrive late, but they also forgot their documents.
tip: мало того что (mala tavo chto = not only that) sets up an added point, often paired with ещё и (yeshchyo i = and also).

english: The city where I was born is small.
tip: For places, где (gde = where) can replace в котором (v katoram): город, где я родился (gorad, gde ya radilsya = the city where I was born).

target: Не забывай тех, кто тебе помог.
english: Don't forget those who helped you.
tip: After кто (kto = who) the verb stays singular even for many people: тех, кто помог (tekh, kto pamog = those who helped), not помогли (pamagli).

target: Она говорила так, словно знала всё.
english: She spoke as if she knew everything.
tip: словно (slovna = as if) introduces an unreal comparison: говорила так, словно знала всё (gavarila tak, slovna znala vsyo = spoke as if she knew everything).
